notes:
Summary: Beryl runs real-time customer-engagement features for an enterprise telco. Primary ask: dedicated GPU pools with predictable throughput and regional failover headroom. Key metrics and asks: 
- Workloads: low-latency session chat + on-call assistant + per-call reranking. Typical request size 128 tokens; bursts up to 800 concurrent sessions regionally.
- Throughput/targets: target sustained throughput ~200 req/s per region, burst tolerant to 400 req/s for 30s windows. Concurrency target ~1k active sessions across regions.
- Latency SLOs: p95 <= 80ms, p99 goal <= 140ms (requesting Redwood concession to 180ms on cold-starts).
- Reserved GPU planning: initial ask = 40 A100-equivalent GPUs split us-east:18, us-west:12, eu-west:10. Require 20-30% failover headroom for region outage and AZ failures. Want recommendations for minimum active set vs. hot spare pool.
- Failover model: active-active routing preferred; cross-region failover with traffic shaping. Need warm KV-cache migration strategy and cold-start mitigation plan.
- Routing/fallback: prefer automatic fallback to quantized variants for cost-limited tiers; want guaranteed routing policy for enterprise traffic (no spill to public pool).
- SLA negotiation points: 99.95% per-region uptime, 95th/99th latency credit triggers, 4hr P1 response, 24/7 support, monthly usage reports. Request 10% credit on monthly invoice for missed p99 windows > 5m.
- Security/compliance: SSO (SAML), audit logging retention 13 months, KMS integration for keys, EU data residency for eu-west pool.
- Economics: prefer 12-month reserved commitment with quarterly review. Target ARR range $250k-$500k based on model/quantization mix.
- Internal sentiment: CTO wants hard throughput guarantees; infra leads worried about cross-region networking cost. Procurement asked for clear failure-mode appendix.
Notes from call: 'We need to be sure our customer messages don't see >200ms p99. That's our customer SLA.' — VP of Product.
Open: confirm A100-equivalent mapping to Redwood instance types; finalize failover headroom percent; POC schedule and procurement timeline.
